discussion_comments.comment_body: This has been addressed. The `catch` block has been updated to explicitly call `controller.error(err)` and we added `errored = true` state tracking to securely and cleanly abort the stream.
This is fixed now. We are explicitly calling `controller.error(err)` in the `catch` block to ensure the error is properly propagated.

Done in 6c73fa14 — classifier now checks `(err as { code?: string }).code` first (`ECONNREFUSED` / `UND_ERR*` prefix) and falls back to the substring match for errors that lack a structured code. Kept the substring branch as a safety net since some undici versions throw plain `Error("fetch failed")` without a code — but agreed that code-based matching is more stable as the primary path.

Agree — fixed in 97ad78cb. Wrapped the per-frame work (zlib + processFrame) in its own try/catch and advance `pos += 5 + length` regardless, so a corrupted frame is logged + skipped instead of looping forever on the same offset. The safety timer is no longer the only escape.
Applied in commit `e104d25`. The route now uses `catch (err: unknown)` plus explicit narrowing before reading the message, so this no longer relies on `any` or unsafe property access.

Fixed in commit `582c54e1`. Wrapped the ROLLBACK in its own try/catch — if rollback throws (transaction already ended, backend in bad state), the original error from the try block is preserved instead of being shadowed by a rollback failure.

Good catch — fixed in commit ce54f5db. The original handler defaulted to `valid: true` for any 403 whose body didn't match the auth regex, which would accept generic `403 Forbidden`, entitlement 403s, geo 403s, etc. Inverted the default: auth-shaped 403 still maps to the re-paste hint, and any other 403 now returns `valid: false` with the upstream body sliced into the error so the cause is visible (e.g. if upstream renames the probe model, the user sees "Model is not found" rather than a misleading 'valid' verdict). Added two new tests covering model-not-found-403 and generic-Forbidden-403, both asserting `valid: false`.

Fixed in c2eae5911. Runtime reads now fall back to the default IDE profile for any non-canonical value, so corrupted persisted data cannot crash request execution, discovery, or the connection editor. Strict write validation still accepts only `ide`/`cli`, and migration 121 still converts known legacy `harness`/`sdk` values to `cli`; the fallback does not restore either legacy alias. Verified with the focused Antigravity regression set (333/333), core typecheck, Prettier, and ESLint.

Addressed in 53007ed99. The fallback now receives only the remaining portion of the original timeout budget, and is skipped when the primary catalog probe has already exhausted that budget. I also switched the primary probe to the official `--list-models` flag so older CLIs fail fast instead of potentially treating an unknown positional `models` subcommand as a prompt.
